artifacts.summary: 6-phase implementation: generalized bimodal's persistent-search-solver re-assertion into the shared ConstraintGenerator base class, added live model-level regression coverage, and documented the residual stored_solver ordering; full iterate/ suite improved from 2 failed/239 passed to 247 passed/0 failed.

next_steps: Task 215 is fully implemented and verified. A dependent task can now verify its own Phase 3 pin-routing blocker has cleared for logos/imposition, since the persistent search solver is genuinely populated (already observed as a passing side effect in iterate/tests/integration/test_models.py::TestGenericPinningReachesRebuiltSolve).

memory_candidates.content: In the ModelChecker Z3 stack, iterate/constraints.py's ConstraintGenerator._create_persistent_solver built the live iteration loop's persistent search solver by copying assertions() off the original model structure's solver, which was empty for every theory lacking a bimodal-style workaround (logos, exclusion, imposition) -- confirmed len(solver.assertions()) == 0 immediately after construction. Fix: generalize bimodal's theory-local re-assertion pattern (theory_lib/bimodal/iterate.py's _ensure_frame_constraints_in_search_solver) up into the shared ConstraintGenerator base class -- a new _ensure_original_constraints_in_solver() method, called from __init__ right after _create_persistent_solver(), reads model_constraints' four component lists directly (frame_constraints/model_constraints/premise_constraints/conclusion_constraints, NOT all_constraints) and re-asserts them, guarded by isinstance(value, list) so Mock() test doubles contribute nothing, and skipped on the CVC5 reused-solver path (tracked via a _reused_original_solver flag) to avoid duplicate assertion. A regression test asserting only len(assertions()) > 0 is insufficient -- it would pass against a still-broken engine, since _setup_solver's assert_tracked calls make a POPULATED solver's assertions() return Implies(label, constraint) tracking implications, which are vacuously satisfiable when copied into a fresh solver. The real acceptance criterion must be model-level: check() the persistent solver, require sat, and verify model.eval() on every real constraint returns true.

In the ModelChecker repo's bimodal theory test suite, theory_lib/bimodal/tests/integration/test_iterate.py::TestLiveIteration::test_a_live_run_detects_a_genuine_rotation_permutation_duplicate is a known-flaky test: it depends on Z3 actually re-visiting an already-seen orbit during a bounded, heuristic-driven search, which is not guaranteed by construction (the test's own docstring documents this). It reliably passes standalone (29/29 every time observed) but intermittently fails only inside the much larger, longer-running four-theory combined pytest gate (logos+exclusion+imposition+bimodal together), independent of unrelated code changes -- confirmed via a controlled A/B where reverting an unrelated fix did not change the failure's presence/absence. When investigating an apparent regression here, always compare the standalone bimodal/tests/integration/test_iterate.py run first before concluding a code change caused it.

reflection.what_worked: The planning-time verification (isolated Z3 repro proving assert_and_track copies are vacuously satisfiable) made the strong, model-level regression test obvious and correct on the first attempt -- RED/GREEN both demonstrated cleanly. Staging the RED capture before applying the fix (via a targeted git stash of just constraints.py) kept the RED evidence honest without losing the already-drafted fix.
reflection.what_was_hard: Phase 4's official four-theory-gate run showed one bimodal test failure that looked like a fix-induced regression at first glance. Distinguishing genuine regression from pre-existing flakiness required a controlled A/B (reverting the fix, re-running the identical gate command twice in each condition) rather than trusting a single capture -- a single pass/fail comparison against Phase 1's baseline was not sufficient evidence either way.
reflection.what_was_missed: None identified -- the plan's own risk table had already anticipated both the bimodal double-assertion risk and the 'newly-constrained search finds fewer models' risk, so no scope was missed, only the investigation effort to confirm which anticipated risk (if any) was actually in play.
reflection.successes: Full iterate/ suite went from 2 failed/239 passed to 247 passed/0 failed, with the two newly-passing tests being another task's own generic-pinning regression tests for logos/imposition -- a side effect the task description explicitly predicted and this task's evidence corroborates without touching that task's own file territory.
